items.t: Apple Looks Very Smart in Modest AI Spend: Tom Forte
items.d: Tom Forte of Maxim Group says he is especially interested in commentary on the December quarter, when the latest iPhone models will have had more time to affect sales. He said initial demand for the new iPhone duo appears strong and pointed to pent-up interest in a foldable iPhone after a long wait. He speaks with Kailey Leinz & Ed Ludlow on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: iPhone Duo Sales To Hit 7M in 2026, Predicts IDC Sr. Director
items.d: IDC Senior Director of Data & Analytics Nabila Popal says Apple’s iPhone results beating analyst expectations were not surprising. IDC’s preliminary shipment data showed iPhones outperforming a smartphone market that had suffered a historic 21% decline in calendar Q3, while Apple’s shipments fell only 4%. She speaks with Kailey Leinz & Ed Ludlow on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: KAIST, AI가 전문지식 학습하는 시간 70% 단축
items.d: 인공지능(AI)에 의료나 코딩 등 전문 지식을 가르치는 데 걸리는 시간을 최대 70% 줄일 수 있는 기술이 개발됐다. AI가 비슷한 내용을 반복 학습하지 않도록 학습 자료를 골라주는 방식이다. KAIST는 전산학부 이재길 교수 연구팀이 AI의 추가 학습 시간을 단축하는 기술 ‘클러스터(CluSTER)’를 개발했다고 2일 밝혔다. AI를 의료 상담이나 프로그램 개발 등 특정 분야에 활용하려면 해당 분야의 자료를 추가로 학습시켜야 한다. 이때 여러 그래픽처리장치(GPU)가 자료를 나눠 학습하는데, 비슷한 내용을 중복해서 처리하면 시간과 비용이 낭비된다. 연구팀은 각 자료가 AI 학습에 미치는 영향을 분석해 비슷한 효과를 내는 자료끼리 묶었다. 이후 중복 학습을 줄이면서도 AI가 여러 종류의 지식을 골고루 익힐

items.t: Web host Squarespace lays off 19% of its employees
items.d: The website builder said that the job losses are part of a broader restructuring of its organization.
items.fullText: Squarespace, the web company that helps customers build and host their own websites, is laying off about one-fifth of its workforce, in a move that will affect hundreds of jobs. Jeff Seedman, a public relations specialist representing Squarespace, confirmed the layoffs to TechCrunch. The Verge initially reported the layoffs. “Squarespace is restructuring its organization and reducing its global workforce by approximately 19%, representing around 300 employees,” said Seedman. “The changes are intended to simplify how we operate, sharpen our priorities and enable the company to move faster as we position Squarespace for its next phase of growth.” Website building has changed immensely over the last few years as a result of the generative AI boom. “Vibe-coding” website builders, which only require simple prompts from users to spin up functional front-end designs, have largely upended the industry, making it possible for users to create sites with significantly less effort. These kinds of sites have become an increasingly central part of the website-building business. Last year, web host rival Wix bought Base44 for $80 million . Similar offerings, like Lovable, have generated significant investor interest; Lovable raised a $400 million Series C round in August that valued the company at $13.3 billion. Google also recently launched Stitch , a feature that allows users to swiftly generate user-interface designs. Squarespace has also begun a big push into AI. In 2024, the company launched an AI tool called Blueprint. The company also recently announced Forma, an upcoming AI native platform, whose waitlist users can join . Squarespace was founded in 2004 and went public in 2021 at a $10 billion valuation. However, the company struggled in the ensuing years to generate enthusiastic public market interest. Squarespace ultimately decided to go private again by way of a $7 billion private equity deal in 2024. An earlier version of this report

items.t: SpaceX reportedly wants to buy Boost Mobile to compete with AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon
items.d: SpaceX has been looking for new ways to use its Starlink network, and a tie-up with cellular operator Boost Mobile could give it the terrestrial access it needs.
items.fullText: SpaceX is looking to buy Boost Mobile from EchoStar, according to a report from The Washington Post. If the deal goes through, it would help the Elon Musk-owned company build a hybrid cellular-satellite network that could help catapult it into fourth place among the top U.S. wireless providers. The space-launch company has been dabbling in cellular connectivity, rolling out satellite access to T-Mobile’s subscribers in 2024. Last year, SpaceX bought $17 billion worth of wireless spectrum from EchoStar for cellular services, which could help the company’s Starlink service reach inside buildings, for example, something it currently struggles with. “This is the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America,” Musk said on X at the time of the spectrum acquisition. Yet, if Musk is still looking to buy access to terrestrial networks, it apparently wasn’t the last piece. Elon Musk, SpaceX’s CEO, reportedly spoke directly with EchoStar chairman Charlie Ergen in October about acquiring Boost Mobile, the mobile virtual network operator. EchoStar has about 7.5 million customers between Boost Mobile and Gen Mobile, its other mobile service offering. Musk has also approached AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon about buying capacity on their networks. All three rejected Musk, and they may still have a say in a SpaceX acquisition of Boost Mobile. Boost doesn’t operate its own towers, instead leasing capacity from AT&T and T-Mobile, which might need to approve such a deal. Sources speaking to The Post said that network leases are usually nontransferable. The big three providers each have over 100 million subscribers, dwarfing Boost Mobile. But while the acquisition would give SpaceX an immediate bump in subscribers, the true value of the deal would be giving the company access to terrestrial cellular networks. items.t: Northwood Space raises $375M Series C at a $2B valuation from a16z and DFJ Growth
items.d: Space infrastructure company Northwood Space on Monday said it had raised $375 million in a Series C round co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and DFJ Growth, valuing the company at $2 billion.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 6:22 AM PST · November 2, 2026 Image Credits: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg / Getty Images Dominic-Madori Davis Northwood Space raises $375M Series C at a $2B valuation from a16z and DFJ Growth Space infrastructure company Northwood Space on Monday said it had raised $375 million in a Series C round co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and DFJ Growth, valuing the company at $2 billion. Founded in 2022, Northwood builds antennas, software, and other technologies that help satellites communicate better with Earth. Bridgit Mendler, co-founder and former actress, serves as its CEO. The company last raised a $100 million Series B in January, also co-led by Andreessen Horowitz, along with a nearly $50 million contract with the U.S. Space Force to upgrade the nation’s “satellite control network,” TechCrunch previously reported. This latest round also includes a financial agreement with HSBC that, along with the funding, will be used to scale the company, hire, and fulfill existing contracts, the startup said.
